display.title: Episode 430: The Two Voices (After Shavuos)
display.summary_short: After Shavuos: the Tikkun, flowers and dairy foods; three sisters from California lead the Shema; Sarah hears two voices over a dime on Shabbos; and a Modeh Ani song.
display.summary_long: Right after Shavuos, Uncle Yossi recalls its customs: reading the Tikkun all through the first night, hearing the Ten Commandments, decorating shul and home with flowers like those near Har Sinai, and eating dairy foods and cheesecake, because Har Sinai is called Har Gavnunim and because the Jewish people, newly given the laws of kashrus, could at first eat only dairy. He urges children to keep their 'Naaseh v'nishma' resolutions. After the Hakochainik march, three sisters visiting from California lead the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time, tied to learning Pirkei Avos through the summer, is about fighting the yetzer hara. On Shabbos afternoon, Sarah finds a dime on the sidewalk and hears two voices: one says it is just a little sin, the other reminds her it is Shabbos. Her father explains with a parable about a beggar who cut a small rope in a rich man's attic and brought a great chandelier crashing down: there is no such thing as a small sin. Mitzvah time reviews 'Shivisi' and Modeh Ani and plays a Modeh Ani song, followed by Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: There is no such thing as a small sin: listen to the yetzer tov, not the yetzer hara.

date.note: 'Right after Chag HaShavuos'; candles 8:07, Shabbos ends 9:18 fit Friday 8 June 1990. One week after Erev Shavuos episode 429.

relations.note: Same story, another telling: 'Episode 1: The Two Voices' (episode 1, 7:59-19:38), told by Rabbi Yosef Goldstein (Uncle Yossi).

quality.notes: Very quiet source. The dramatized 'two voices' scenes (about 13:10-17:30) are only partly transcribed, likely voices over music. The guests' Shema, the march and the Modeh Ani song are not transcribed.
